# Sitakunda shrouded in fog, shipbreaking work continues


The Sitakunda coast in Chattogram was shrouded in a blanket of fog early in the morning. Ignoring the poor visibility, workers remained busy with shipbreaking activities from the morning. 
Old ships are dismantled here, meeting a significant portion of the country’s demand for steel.

Chattogram

Published : 16 August 2026

•

Updated : 16 August 2026, 09:30

• [BANGLADESH
dying?](https://www.thedailystar.net/opinion/views/news/if-shipbreaking-regulated-why-are-workers-still-dying-4248441) According to the Bangladesh Ship Breakers and Recyclers Association (BSBRA), 23 
“green yards” are currently operating, with eight more undergoing trial operations. Accident data show that incidents continue to occur repeatedly at certified facilities. 
KR Steel Yard in Lalbagh, Sitakunda, recorded the highest number, with 29 accidents leaving 29 workers injured. 
Arefin Enterprise recorded nine accidents, leaving eight injured and one dead; Ferdous Steel recorded four, leaving nine dead and 10 injured; and Janata Steel recorded six, among others.
